# remove-bg

Imported as `@elffuss/ai/remove-bg`, `@elffuss/ai/remove-bg/sizes`.

## `sdk/remove-bg/index.js`

Remove the background of an image in the browser: a PNG with transparency at the size of the input, and its mask. The model is BEN2 (MIT, by PramaLLC), downloaded once from its pinned Hugging Face repository through the Elffuss model store; it runs in a Worker, on WebAssembly.

### Type `RemoveBgResult`

```ts
{ png: Blob, width: number, height: number, alpha: Uint8Array, device: 'webgpu'|'wasm', scaled: boolean, sourceWidth: number, sourceHeight: number, coverage: number }
```

`png` is the image with the background made transparent, `width` × `height` pixels: the input's size, or the scaled-down size when the input was larger than `maxSide` (`scaled` true, the input's own size in `sourceWidth` × `sourceHeight`). `alpha` is the PNG's alpha channel, one byte per pixel, row by row. `coverage` is the share of pixels kept (alpha of 128 or more), from 0 to 1.

### `class RemoveBg`

Background removal with BEN2. Loads once (concurrent calls share the load),
runs one image after another, and runs the model in a Worker that is replaced
after any failure. Options: `device` ('auto' or 'wasm'; the model declares no
WebGPU variant, so 'webgpu' fails with `device-unsupported`), `onProgress`,
`signal`, and the store and registry overrides of `TaskOptions`.

    import { RemoveBg } from '@elffuss/ai/remove-bg'
    const remover = new RemoveBg({ onProgress: p => console.log(p.status, p.loaded, p.total) })
    const { png, width, height, alpha, device } = await remover.run(file)
    img.src = URL.createObjectURL(png)       // same size as the file, transparent background
    await remover.dispose()

- `.constructor(options)`
- `.run(input, opts)`: Remove the background of one image. Accepts a Blob or File (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, BMP or AVIF, by its first bytes), an ImageBitmap, an ImageData, or an image, canvas or video element (turned into an ImageBitmap here). EXIF orientation is applied. Fails with `decode-failed`, `unsupported-format`, `too-large`, `aborted` or `run-failed`.

### `removeBg`

Load the model, remove the background of one image, and release the model.
Takes the options of RemoveBg and of its run in one object.

## `sdk/remove-bg/mask.js`

The image maths of background removal, with no browser API so that Node tests them: the model input (the photo resized to the model's square with PIL's bilinear filter, which averages every pixel when it shrinks instead of sampling a few, then normalised as the model's preprocessor config says), the mask brought back to the photo's size, and the alpha put on the photo's pixels. The same numbers come out on every browser and backend: nothing here goes through a canvas.

### `MAX_SIDE`

Largest side the task processes; a larger image is scaled down to it first.

### `resampleWeights(inSize, outSize)`

Coefficients of a one-dimensional resampling with PIL's bilinear filter: a
triangle one pixel wide when enlarging (plain bilinear, pixel centres at
half-integers, as `align_corners=False`) and as wide as the scale when
shrinking, so that every input pixel counts. Each row sums to 1.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `inSize` | `number` |  |
| `outSize` | `number` |  |

Returns `{ start: Int32Array, count: Int32Array, weights: Float32Array, ksize: number }`.

### `resamplePlane(src, w, h, ow, oh)`

Resample a single-channel plane (any numeric array) to another size.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `src` | `ArrayLike<number>` |  |
| `w` | `number` |  |
| `h` | `number` |  |
| `ow` | `number` |  |
| `oh` | `number` |  |

Returns `Float32Array`.

### `inputSpec(processor)`

What the model takes, read from its image processor (Transformers.js reads it
from preprocessor_config.json): the square size, and the rescale and
normalisation it was trained with.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `processor` | `{ size?: { width?: number, height?: number }\|number, image_mean?: number[]\|number, image_std?: number[]\|number, rescale_factor?: number, do_rescale?: boolean, do_normalize?: boolean, do_resize?: boolean }` |  |

Returns `{ width: number, height: number, mean: number[], std: number[], rescale: number }`.

### `toModelInput({ data, width, height }, { width: W, height: H, mean, std, rescale })`

The model input: RGBA pixels resized to the model's size and normalised, as
a planar (channels first) Float32Array: (value · rescale − mean) / std.
The alpha the image may have is not read: the model sees the colours.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `img` | `{ data: ArrayLike<number>, width: number, height: number }` | RGBA, 8 bits per channel |
| `spec` | `{ width: number, height: number, mean: number[], std: number[], rescale: number }` |  |

Returns `Float32Array`: 3 × spec.height × spec.width values

### `maskToAlpha(mask, mw, mh, ow, oh)`

The model's output, at the image's size, as alpha (0-255). Values outside
0-1 are taken as logits and pass through a sigmoid first, as the
Transformers.js segmentation pipeline does; anything that is not a number
means the run went wrong.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `mask` | `ArrayLike<number>` | mw × mh values |
| `mw` | `number` |  |
| `mh` | `number` |  |
| `ow` | `number` |  |
| `oh` | `number` |  |

Returns `Uint8Array`.

### `applyAlpha(rgba, alpha)`

Put the mask on RGBA pixels, in place. Where the image already had some
transparency it stays: the result is mask × the image's own alpha. `alpha`
is updated to what the pixels end up with, so it is the PNG's alpha channel.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `rgba` | `Uint8ClampedArray\|Uint8Array` |  |
| `alpha` | `Uint8Array` |  |

Returns `Uint8ClampedArray\|Uint8Array`: rgba

### `coverage(alpha, threshold = 128)`

Share of the pixels the cut keeps (alpha at least `threshold`), from 0 to 1.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `alpha` | `Uint8Array` |  |
| `[threshold]` | `number` |  |

### `sideLimit(maxSide)`

The longest side the task decodes at: the caller's `maxSide` when it is a
positive integer below MAX_SIDE, else MAX_SIDE.
